subject: Art & Design
title: Gutenberg and the Printing Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply Gutenberg and the Printing Revolution.

hook.text: Before 1440, every book in Europe was copied by hand. One monk, one book, months of work.

buildup.text: Gutenberg combined movable metal type with a wine press. The printing press was born.

discovery.text: His first major print — the Gutenberg Bible — used blackletter type mimicking handwritten manuscripts.

twist.text: Gutenberg went bankrupt. His investor seized the press and made the fortune instead.

climax.text: Within 50 years, 20 million books were printed in Europe. Literacy, science, and revolution followed.

punchline.text: One press. Twenty million books. The world was never the same.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about Gutenberg's invention?
options: Movable metal type enabled mass production of books

details.summary: Johannes Gutenberg's invention of movable metal type around 1440 revolutionized information distribution. His printing press made books affordable, democratized knowledge, fueled the Reformation, and established typographic conventions — justified text, columns.
details.whyItMatters: Gutenberg's press was the most transformative communication technology before the internet. Understanding this origin explains why typographic conventions exist and reveals typography's deep connection to the spread of knowledge and power.
takeaways: Gutenberg invented movable metal type around 1440
The press democratized knowledge and fueled the Reformation
Conventions established then still influence typography today

faq.question: What was the Gutenberg Bible?
faq.answer: Gutenberg's first major printed work (1455), a Latin Bible produced in about 180 copies. It demonstrated that printed text could rival handwritten manuscripts in beauty while being produced far faster.

faq.question: Did Gutenberg profit from his invention?
faq.answer: No. His investor Johann Fust sued him for unpaid debts, took control of his workshop and printing equipment, and completed the Bible project himself. Gutenberg died in relative obscurity. The pattern of inventors losing control of revolutionary technologies is as old as Gutenberg himself.
